## Natural history notes

A medium-sized grass skipper characterized by its long, narrow brown wings, pale translucent spots on the forewings, and fast darting flight. In Florida, it is common in open grassy habitats such as prairies, roadsides, lawns, marsh edges, fields, gardens, and disturbed areas where grasses and nectar plants are abundant. Adults visit flowers for nectar and often rest with wings partly open, while the caterpillars feed on grasses, using folded or tied grass blades as shelters during development.
